description: We are a team of five innovative members striving to fill the gap in the world of space-themed games. Our team stands out for its strong problem-solving skills, digital game design expertise, and ability to collaborate effectively. Together, we aim to bring creative ideas to life and develop unique gaming experiences.
summary:
We developed EXOVIA: An interactive 3D educational game that puts players in the role of a space mission designer.
Space mission design is complex, requiring careful balance between scientific goals, engineering constraints, and strict budgets. EXOVIA addresses this challenge by breaking the process down into four accessible, hands-on phases: mission selection, spacecraft selection, real-time 3D spacecraft design, and orbit selection. Through color-coded requirement trackers, launch confidence percentages, and constructive feedback after failed launches, players learn space engineering through trial and error rather than passive instruction.
This project is important because it connects space technology directly to Bahrain’s local environmental needs. Such as, protecting coastlines, mangroves, and coral reefs, while inspiring young Bahrainis to explore STEM and space careers. Ultimately, EXOVIA transforms complex aerospace concepts into an engaging platform that fuels curiosity and prepares the next generation of space explorers.
details:
What Does It Do & How Does It Work?

EXOVIA is an interactive, browser-based 3D space mission design game where players step into the role of aerospace systems engineers solving real-world environmental challenges from orbit.

Modeled on real NASA mission architecture across the Space, Launch, Ground, and User segments, players progress through a four-step engineering workflow:

  1. Select a Mission (User Segment): Choose between Global Weather Analysis (spanning 6 climate regions: Arabian Gulf, Sahara, Monsoon Asia, Sahel, Caribbean, and Pacific Islands) and three hyper-local environmental missions in the Kingdom of Bahrain: Coastal Guardian, Mangrove Conservation, and Coral Reef Protector.
  2. Choose a Spacecraft Bus (Space Segment): Select between an Earth-Orbiting Satellite (60 kg payload capacity for continuous monitoring) or a Flyby Spacecraft (52 kg payload capacity for single-pass observation).
  3. Engineer the Payload & Subsystems (Space & Ground Segments): Equip up to 16 NASA-inspired remote-sensing instruments (such as Synthetic Aperture Radar, Aerosol Lidar, Radar Altimeters, and Hyperspectral Imagers) alongside power and communications upgrades (Extended Solar Arrays and High-Gain Antennas for ground-station downlink). Players must balance a $10.0M starting budget and strict payload mass limits while collecting the exact 15 environmental datasets required by their chosen mission.
  4. Pick an Orbit & Launch (Launch Segment): Select an orbital trajectory (e.g., 700 km Sun-Synchronous Polar Orbit vs. 35,786 km Geostationary Orbit) based on spatial resolution needs, then watch a real-time 3D rocket launch from liftoff through Max-Q, stage separation, and orbital deployment. Mission success awards a +$1.0M bonus to fund subsequent builds.

What Benefits Does It Have?

  • End-to-End Mission Architecture Literacy: Players experience how NASA structures real missions across the Launch, Space, Ground, and User segments, learning why high-gain antennas, solar arrays, orbital altitudes, and sensor wavelengths all depend on one another.
  • Hands-On Systems Engineering: Rather than passively reading technical manuals, users actively balance budget constraints, mass limits, instrument capabilities, and launch risk through immediate 3D visual feedback.
  • Zero-Barrier Classroom & Public Access: Packaged inside a single self-contained HTML file with no installations, logins, or external asset downloads, EXOVIA runs instantly on any laptop, tablet, or smartphone.

What Is the Intended Impact of the Project?

  • Connecting Space Science to Local Communities: By pairing global weather forecasting with dedicated missions protecting the Kingdom of Bahrain’s coastlines, mangrove bays, and coral reefs, EXOVIA shows how orbital Earth-observation data directly protects local ecosystems and coastal infrastructure.
  • Inspiring Future Aerospace Engineers: EXOVIA demystifies early-stage mission formulation—mirroring concepts from NASA’s Mission Design Lab (MDL) and CubeSat 101—so students (ages 12+) and educators can experience how real space missions are built through smart engineering compromises.

What Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, Software, & Resources Did You Use?

Coding Languages & Core Web Technologies

  • Languages: HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+).
  • 3D Graphics & Rendering: Three.js (WebGL) for real-time 3D rendering of Earth, procedural continents/clouds, modular spacecraft assembly, orbital trajectories, and multi-stage rocket launches.
  • Procedural Audio: Web Audio API for real-time synthesized soundscapes, mechanical instrument snaps, rocket ignition roars, and telemetry pings with zero external audio files.

AI & Creative Production Tools

  • Gemini, Claude, & ChatGPT: Assisted with code architecture, procedural 3D shader/audio refinement, mission balancing, and educational copywriting.
  • Gamma: Used to design and structure our team’s pitch presentation deck.
  • Flow: Used to generate our cinematic 30-second mission trailer showcasing Bahrain’s environmental challenges and EXOVIA’s gameplay loop.

Official NASA & Space Apps Challenge Resources Used

  • Mission Architecture & Systems Engineering: Design and Develop Science Missions, Launch Segment, Space Segment, Ground Segment, and User Segment (used to structure our four-phase gameplay loop, ground downlink mechanics, and end-user environmental objectives).
  • Early-Stage Mission Formulation: Concept Maturity Levels (CMLs), Mission Design Lab (MDL), and CubeSat 101 – Basic Concepts and Processes for First-Time CubeSat Developers (used to model small-satellite mass constraints, rapid trade-study iteration, and subsystem budgeting).
  • Orbital Mechanics & Visualization: General Mission Analysis Tool (GMAT), NASA Mission Viz, and Visualize a Space Mission Using Virtual Reality (used as inspiration for our 3D orbital trajectory rings, altitude-vs-resolution trade-offs, and interactive spacecraft inspection camera).
  • Educational Game Design: A Learning Game About Telescopes and NASA Digital Games and Activities (used to guide how we translate complex optical/sensor physics into intuitive, approachable gameplay).

How Is Your Project Creative?

  • 100% Procedural 3D & Audio Engine: Every planet, cloud layer, starfield, spacecraft instrument mesh, and sound effect is generated mathematically in real time inside a single lightweight HTML file, requiring zero external 3D models or audio downloads.
  • Hyper-Local Meets Global Storytelling: Linking international climate hazards directly to localized environmental protection in the Kingdom of Bahrain creates an immediate, personal connection to space data.
  • Realistic Launch Risk & "Distractor" Science: Capping launch confidence at 96% to reflect real-world rocket risk (Max-Q and stage separation) and including valid-but-irrelevant instruments (such as the Magnetometer) challenges players to think critically like real mission planners rather than buying parts blindly.

What Factors Did Your Team Consider?

  • Scientific Authenticity vs. Playability: Guided by CubeSat 101 and Mission Design Lab principles, we scaled real instrument mass, cost, and orbital resolution trade-offs into balanced numbers so a complete mission can be designed and launched in under five minutes.
  • Clarity & Onboarding: To ensure non-engineers aren't overwhelmed by aerospace terminology, we created a guided 4-step workflow, color-coded dataset tags, plain-language hover tooltips, and a live "Mission Needs" checklist.
  • Performance & Accessibility: We capped WebGL pixel ratios for smooth mobile and desktop performance, built responsive CSS layouts, added ARIA/keyboard focus support, and implemented prefers-reduced-motion checks for motion-sensitive users.
